WITHDRAWAL_after_review_316625.WITHDRAWN: all of it. The reviewer read the source and every objection is correct; I have re-read the same source and confirmed each one rather than taking it on trust.
WITHDRAWAL_after_review_316625.and_--once_still_omits_the_reclaim: confirmed again: `_serve` returns `reconcile(...)` for `--once` and wires `_reclaiming(...)` only on the persistent path.
WITHDRAWAL_after_review_316625.what_I_claimed: "the command is runnable today and, run as it stands, reaches the HELD outcome", with `tools.job_manager serve` presented as THE supported disposition and "stop it with ONE Ctrl-C once its pass has reported".
why_it_was_wrong: IT IS NOT BOUNDED OR TARGET-SPECIFIC. `manager.serve` runs `reconcile(...)` once and then, every tick, `sleep(interval)`, `sweep(...)` and only THEN the reclaim -- the source says so and says why: 'once per tick, AFTER the ordinary sweep, so a reclaim never races the launch pass in the same tick'. The ordinary sweep IS that launch pass. So this entry can resume normal Job action -- offers, claims, starts -- outside any supervisor limit this campaign selected, on an instance whose Job is spent and whose review is held. Nothing about it is scoped to one attempt.

THE STOPPING INSTRUCTION WAS CIRCULAR. `serve` answers only its LAST report, after the loop stops -- 'Answers the LAST report rather than every one of them'. So an operator cannot see whether the reclaim ran, let alone what it answered, until after deciding to stop; 'stop once its pass has reported' asks for an observation the entry does not provide until it has already ended.

A RECLAIM REFUSAL ENDS THE RUN. The source is explicit -- 'its refusals are not swallowed ... and ends the run' -- so one refused attempt stops the whole serving process, which is a further effect an operator is owed in advance.

THE TEMPLATE LEFT TWO OPERANDS UNRESOLVED. `PYTHONPATH=<staged>/src:<staged>` names no actual tree -- each run staged its own, and the current helper digests no longer match those retained manifests -- and `--custodian-image` had no value at all.
